indicators.section: Financial Red Flags Relating to Mail Theft-Related Check Fraud
indicators.flag: Non-characteristic large withdrawals on a customer’s account via check to a new payee.
indicators.red_flag: Out-of-pattern large check withdrawal to a new payee

indicators.red_flag: Customer-reported mail-stolen check deposited to unknown account
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D6 (Check / negotiable-instrument image & metadata), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: Customer complains that a check they mailed was never received by the intended recipient.

indicators.section: Financial Red Flags Relating to Mail Theft-Related Check Fraud
indicators.flag: Checks used to withdraw funds from a customer’s account appear to be of a noticeably different check stock than check stock used by the issuing bank and check stock used for known, legitimate transactions.
indicators.red_flag: Counterfeit check-stock mismatch vs. issuer / legitimate baseline
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D6 (Check / negotiable-instrument image & metadata), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Financial Red Flags Relating to Mail Theft-Related Check Fraud
indicators.flag: Existing customer with no history of check deposits has new sudden check deposits and withdrawal or transfer of funds.
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C6 (Transaction-velocity & dormancy / baseline-deviation monitoring).

indicators.section: Financial Red Flags Relating to Mail Theft-Related Check Fraud
indicators.flag: Non-characteristic, sudden, abnormal deposit of checks, often electronically, followed by rapid withdrawal or transfer of funds.
indicators.red_flag: Abnormal remote check deposit → rapid pass-through withdrawal
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C2 (Rapid pass-through / flow-through (receive-and-forward) detection).

indicators.section: Financial Red Flags Relating to Mail Theft-Related Check Fraud
indicators.flag: Examination of suspect checks reveals faded handwriting underneath darker handwriting, giving the appearance that the original handwriting has been overwritten.
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D6 (Check / negotiable-instrument image & metadata), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Financial Red Flags Relating to Mail Theft-Related Check Fraud
indicators.flag: Suspect accounts may have indicators of other suspicious activity, such as pandemic-related fraud.
indicators.red_flag: Co-occurring suspicious activity (e.g. pandemic-relief fraud) on suspect account
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C1 (Customer-profile / out-of-pattern transaction monitoring); data D1.

indicators.section: Financial Red Flags Relating to Mail Theft-Related Check Fraud
indicators.flag: New customer opens an account that is seemingly used only for the deposit of checks followed by frequent withdrawals and transfer of funds.
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C13 (Account-opening / KYC risk profiling).

indicators.section: Financial Red Flags Relating to Mail Theft-Related Check Fraud
indicators.flag: A non-customer that is attempting to cash a large check or multiple large checks in-person and, when questioned by the financial institution, provides an explanation that is suspicious or potentially indicative of money mule activity.
indicators.red_flag: Non-customer in-person large-check cashing with mule-indicative explanation
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D6 (Check / negotiable-instrument image & metadata), not currently held → source data first.
